date_note: The Record's article of 25 November gives no earlier day for FIFA's confirmation; it says the group claimed the attack 'last week'.
exec: FIFA says hackers accessed a limited set of personal and business information, a reminder that sports bodies are targets too.
plain: FIFA says hackers got into a limited set of personal and business information. A hacking group says it was behind it and has published data; FIFA says it is working with law enforcement.

sources.name: Meduza (Russian): FIFA hit by cyberattack; hackers claim to have stolen data

summary: FIFA told The Record that hackers gained unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information, and that it is working with the relevant authorities. The Record reports a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club claimed the attack and published stolen data on a cybercriminal forum; those claims are unverified. FIFA did not respond to follow-ups. EFE (via rtvc.es) reports FIFA said documents related to FIFA Forward Enterprise were not compromised.
title: FIFA says hackers accessed a 'limited set of personal and business information'

validation.note: The Record and Meduza (citing AP) each report FIFA's statement that hackers accessed a limited set of personal and business information; the group's claims are unverified.

review.note: Compared FIFA statement, unverified HBHC claim, last-week timing, no reply to follow-ups against The Record and Meduza/AP
